Mannucci]] |continentalcup1 = [[2022 Copa Sudamericana|Copa Sudamericana]] |continentalcup1 qualifiers = |num_teams = 30 |matches = 30 |goals = 65 | biggest home win = | biggest away win = | highest scoring = | top goal scorer = [[Yorleys Mena]] (3 goals) | prevseason = [[2019 Copa Bicentenario|2019]] | nextseason = }} The '''2021 Copa Bicentenario''' was the 2nd edition of the [[Copa Bicentenario]], the national cup competition of [[Peru]], with the participation of the 18 teams of the [[Peruvian Primera División|Liga 1]], and 12 teams of the [[Segunda División Peruana|Liga 2]].{{cite web|title=Copa Bicentenario suspendida: ¿Qué pasará con el cupo a la Sudamericana?|url=https://larepublica.pe/deportes/2020/05/11/copa-bicentenario-del-futbol-peruano-suspendida-que-pasara-con-el-cupo-a-la-copa-sudamericana/|editor=La Republica|date=11 May 2020 |access-date=11 May 2020}} The champions qualified for the [[2022 Copa Sudamericana]], as well as the [[Supercopa Peruana]] against the [[2021 Liga 1 (Peru)|Liga 1]] champions. [[Atlético Grau]] were the defending champions. [[Sporting Cristal]] were the winners of the competition, beating [[Carlos A. Mannucci]] in the final by a 2–1 score to claim their first Copa Bicentenario title. == Format == Unlike the previous edition, this year's edition featured a single elimination knockout stage, rather than the group stage. Each team is seeded in the first round, where each team plays one legged games and the winner advances to the final rounds. The final rounds feature a Round of 16, quarter-finals, semi-finals and final. Like the previous round, each match is played in one leg. [[2019 Liga 1 (Peru)|2019 Liga 1]] champions, [[Sporting Cristal]] received a bye to the final rounds. The final is played on a neutral ground in one match. == Schedule == The schedule of the competition was as follows: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center" !Round !First leg |- |First round |10–13 June 2021 |- |Final rounds |16 June – 27 July 2021 |- |Round of 16 |16–20 June 2021 |- |Quarter-finals |23–25 June 2024 |- |Semi-finals |4 July 2021 |- |Final |27 July 2021 |} ==Teams== 18 teams of the [[2021 Liga 1 (Peru)|2021 Liga 1]] and the 12 teams of the [[2021 Liga 2 (Peru)|Liga 2]] participated in the competition. ===Stadia and locations=== {{location map+ |Peru |float=right |width=550 |caption=Locations of the 2021 Liga 1 and Liga 2 teams |places= {{location map~ |Peru |lat=-13.525 |long=-71.972222 |label=
